{{Not to be confused|Archetypal literary criticism}}

'''Archetypal analysis''' in [[statistics]] is an [[unsupervised learning]] method similar to [[cluster analysis]] and introduced by [[Adele Cutler]] and [[Leo Breiman]] in 1994. Rather than "typical" observations (cluster centers), it seeks extremal points in the multidimensional data, the "[[archetype]]s". The archetypes are [[convex combination]]s of observations chosen so that observations can be approximated by convex combinations of the archetypes.

==Literature==
* Adele Cutler and Leo Breiman. Archetypal analysis. Technometrics, 36(4):338–347, November 1994.
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20140829063935/http://www.statistik.lmu.de/~eugster/publications/talk-2012-HIIT-archetypes.pdf Manuel J. A. Eugster: Archetypal Analysis, Mining the Extreme. HIIT seminar, Helsinki Institute for Information Technology, 2012]
* Anil Damle, Yuekai Sun: A geometric approach to archetypal analysis and non-negative matrix factorization. arXiv preprint: [https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.4275 arXiv : 1405.4275]
